name: Banh khot
summary: Bánh khọt is a bite-size cake fried in small molds, crisp outside and soft inside, topped with shrimp or squid and scallion oil. Wrap one in lettuce and herbs and dip it in sweet-sour fish sauce.
origin: Vung Tau, on Nguyễn Trường Tộ and Hoàng Hoa Thám.
culture: Vietnam Tourism calls bánh khọt the snack a Vung Tau trip is incomplete without. Nguyễn Trường Tộ and Hoàng Hoa Thám are the streets to eat it.
texture: The cakes fry in small cast-iron molds until the outside is crisp and the inside soft, then take shrimp or squid, scallions, and scallion oil on top.

Accounts of the batter differ. Vietnam Tourism’s local-eating article and Vietnam Airlines say rice flour, while Vietnam Tourism’s essential guide says flour with curry powder and finishes the cake with shrimp powder.
taste: The dip is sweet-sour fish sauce, with a little mild chili. Vietnam Tourism’s essential guide adds papaya to the sauce.
howToEat: Wrap one cake at a time in lettuce and herbs, then dip it. Keep the sauce on the side rather than pouring it over the stack.
It is a small molded cake, not a folded bánh xèo.
where: Nguyễn Trường Tộ, on the Back Beach side of town. One kitchen at number 14 opens 7:00–14:00 on weekdays and 7:00–20:00 on Sundays.
Hoàng Hoa Thám, the street that leads to the whale hall, is the other bánh khọt street.
seoTitle: Banh khot in Vung Tau — the small crisp cake
seoDescription: Bánh khọt is a small crisp cake fried in molds, topped with shrimp, wrapped in herbs, and dipped in sweet-sour fish sauce. Eat it on Nguyễn Trường Tộ.
